text: This replaces D-0227, which narrowed the ratified D-0218 without a ratification, with #357's second review folded in, so it waits for @gitdek's ratification. A watcher's lease has tenures: each time it takes the lease from somewhere other than where it last left it, as after another watcher held it, a new tenure begins. A step takes effect only in the tenure it started in, since what it read of the issue may be older than another watcher's effects, and an effect outside any step takes none. The one exception is an agent run that outlived its step's tenure while the watcher took the lease back: the watcher records the run's result on the run's own ref, which its own record started, and publishes nothing of it then, and its next step publishes it only if no later post answered or replaced the build, as SPEC said already. A watcher that lost the lease and hasn't taken it back still drops the run (D-0113). A push of the lease that landed but whose answer was lost is the watcher's own: the push reads the lease back and returns its own commit, and when it can't, the watcher remembers exactly what it pushed and adopts a lease that says that, starting a new tenure only if that push took the lease from elsewhere, so a lost answer to a renewal no longer ends every running build. A watcher that comes back from a pause also reads the issue again before it answers a retry, and answers nothing once another watcher answered it or the issue moved on, and before a build's push, pull request and post it checks that no later post answered or replaced the build, and publishes nothing of one that did. A post saying a draft or build stopped partway says the watcher running it stopped or lost the repository's lease, not that the factory stopped. The proved recovery and plan cores still see the lease only as held or not: the tenure check is the watcher's own, before each effect. #357's two reviews found the duplicate answers, stale publishes, lost-answer renewals and unrecorded results these stop.
